chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), he used to say:
"I do not accept as valid, regarding the sighting of the crescent, except the testimony of two just men."
ai.seo_question: What is the required testimony for validating the sighting of the crescent moon in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the testimony of two just (adl) men as the sufficient and exclusive criterion for validating the sighting of the lunar crescent, a ruling foundational to Shia jurisprudence regarding the lunar calendar. This emphasis on 'adalah' (moral integrity) reflects the broader Shia legal principle that personal piety and reliability are paramount in evidentiary matters, distinguishing it from other schools that may accept broader testimony or astronomical calculations. The ruling underscores the importance of communal verification in determining religious obligations such as fasting and Eid.
